summary: The implementation is broad, careful, and verifiably correct on every dimension EXCEPT one: the literal CLI invocation the spec itself names for AT-2893 ('axc test --fuzz examples/fuzz_unsat.axc' with no other flags) does NOT produce the documented UNSATISFIABLE/exit-3 result -- it produces a usage ERROR/exit-2 ('must supply --buffer-sizes or --size') because main.rs::run_test requires --buffer-sizes/--size before ever calling fuzz_kernel (which is where the UNSATISFIABLE short-circuit actually lives, ahead of any buffer-size check). The coder's own AT-2893 unit test bypasses this gap by calling fuzz_kernel() directly with a hand-supplied buffer_sizes vec, so the gap was never caught by the test suite despite the test's 'end_to_end' name. Independently re-run with echo $? per the QA task's explicit instruction: exit=2, not exit=3. This is a real, reproducible, spec-literal discrepancy in a named acceptance test, not a nitpick -- hence FAIL. Every other verification axis (build/clippy/tests, GPU legs on real NVIDIA + Lavapipe, severity-ordering comparator, oracle wiring, LOC honesty, AT-2885/AT-2883 deviations, scope) checks out clean; this is a single, narrow, easily-fixable defect (move the buffer-size usage-gate in main.rs::run_test to AFTER front-end parse + solve(), mirroring fuzz_kernel's own internal ordering -- or special-case UNSATISFIABLE detection to run before the buffer-size gate).
requirements_missing: AT-2893 (fuzz UNSATISFIABLE end-to-end via CLI): the literal spec command 'axc test --fuzz examples/fuzz_unsat.axc' returns verdict ERROR / exit 2 ('must supply --buffer-sizes or --size'), NOT verdict UNSATISFIABLE / exit 3 as the r3/fix-3 spec text and §3.6 mandate. The coder's unit test (fuzz.rs::at_2893_fuzz_unsat_end_to_end_no_gpu_needed) only exercises fuzz_kernel() directly with buffer_sizes:[64] pre-supplied, sidestepping main.rs's CLI-level usage gate -- so this AT is unit-covered but NOT CLI-end-to-end-covered, despite its name. Independently reproduced (see verification_results.cli_hands_on below).

blocking_finding_for_orchestrator.what: AT-2893's literal CLI command ('axc test --fuzz examples/fuzz_unsat.axc') returns ERROR/exit2 instead of the spec-mandated UNSATISFIABLE/exit3, because main.rs::run_test's buffer-size usage gate (line ~189) runs BEFORE any front-end parse/solve() call, whereas fuzz_kernel()'s own internal ordering (correctly) checks solve()/UNSATISFIABLE before touching buffer_sizes at all (fuzz.rs lines 901-926 vs 956-965).

blocking_finding_for_orchestrator.suggested_fix: In main.rs::run_test, defer the buffer_sizes-required usage check until AFTER a cheap front-end parse+lower_module+solve() pass has determined the kernel is not already UNSATISFIABLE by source alone -- mirroring fuzz_kernel's own internal short-circuit order -- OR thread the buffer_sizes-optional path through fuzz_kernel itself (call it with an empty/placeholder buffer_sizes when none was supplied, and let fuzz_kernel's own internal buffer_sizes.len()-mismatch check at line 956 raise the usage error AFTER the solve()-based UNSATISFIABLE check has had first refusal, exactly as it already does when buffer_sizes IS supplied but count-mismatched).
